claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The source says organisations are measuring AI productivity by volume of generated code or content produced by a button click, and calls this trajectory deeply misguided.
claims.quote:
We see a wild rush where organisations measure productivity by "a zillion lines of code" or content generated by a button click.

At Team Topologies, we believe this trajectory is deeply misguided.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The source says AI systems require clearly defined, long-lived responsibility boundaries and highly constrained, structured context, analogous to managing human cognitive load.
claims.quote: Instead, AI systems require clearly defined, long-lived boundaries of responsibility and highly constrained, structured context. Just as humans work best when their cognitive load is managed, AI agents work best when the context injected into their operating window is strictly defined and focused.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The source recommends consuming clean interfaces from a platform so that both human teams and AI agents have their cognitive and contextual loads minimised.
claims.quote: By consuming clean interfaces from the platform, both human teams and AI agents have their cognitive and contextual loads minimised, enabling a safe, rapid flow of value.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The source says long-lived teams acting as strict stewards of value flow ensure that only the smallest, highest-quality, and most secure changes are promoted.
claims.quote: Long-lived teams acting as strict stewards of their value flow ensure that only the smallest, highest-quality, and most secure changes are promoted.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: The source argues AI forces teams to move past construction boundaries and establish stewardship boundaries around value flow and human accountability.
claims.quote: AI forces us to move past "construction boundaries" and instead **establish clear boundaries around the stewardship of value flow and human accountability**.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The source argues code is a liability and that every extra AI-produced line must be tested, maintained, and secured.
claims.quote: In software delivery, code is a liability, not an asset (even if the accountants tell a different story). Every extra line of code produced by an AI is an extra line that must be tested, maintained, and secured.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The source claims that putting more code live enlarges the security attack surface and that flooding production with unverified, AI-generated code exponentially increases security risks.
claims.quote: The more code an organisation puts live, the larger its security attack surface becomes. Threat actors - whether nation-states or dark web syndicates - are constantly looking for vulnerabilities. Flooding production with unverified, AI-generated code exponentially increases security risks.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: The source prescribes end-to-end tiny slices for rapid value flow, deployed safely and quality-verified before iteration, rather than large unverified blocks.
claims.quote: The only approach that works effectively for rapid value flow - with or without AI - is breaking work down into end-to-end tiny slices. Instead of building a massive, unverified block of software/content/data and throwing it over the wall, we must build the smallest possible increment, deploy it safely, verify its quality, and iterate.
